claim: Ignoring what an action undoes (delete relaxation) gives a cheap estimate that guides greedy search well on most planning benchmarks. FF won AIPS-2000; Fast Downward and LAMA, which build on it, won IPC-4 and IPC-2008; under ideal h+, 24 of 30 domains have no unrecognised dead ends.
agent_test: Compare relaxed-then-rank against plain ranking of S3 children at equal tokens; the relaxed step must be cheaper than one extra full attempt.

claim: The relaxed estimate is blind to trouble caused by the constraint that was dropped. FF fails on Mystery and Mprime (fuel dead ends); 6 of 30 domains have unrecognised dead ends (a rover takes a one-off sample, then cannot reach the lander). Random restarts did not fix it. Gap check 2026-10-26: a generated heuristic that ignores object interactions still lost to saturated cost partitioning in 4 of 10 IPC 2023 domains (LeanPlan, d02), and a dead-end test gave the largest single gain (Spanner).
agent_test: Log cases where the relaxed child scored high but the real test failed; if the dropped constraint was the cause, mark it must-recheck before S7 SELECT.

claim: A relaxed solution also yields a free shortlist of next moves (FF helpful actions, Fast Downward preferred operators). FF keeps 40% down to 2% of successors; Fast Downward preferred operators helped in 10 domains vs hurt in 5 (greedy) and helped in 15 vs hurt in 2 (multi-heuristic).
agent_test: Use the first steps of the relaxed solution to restrict which branches are expanded; measure pass rate at a fixed attempt budget.

claim: Relaxation is weak where the order of goals matters. FF's Blocksworld results came mainly from goal ordering, not the relaxed distance; the FF heuristic left 4 of 35 Blocksworld tasks unsolved in Fast Downward's comparison.
agent_test: On order-dependent tasks, test whether an explicit ordering step beats relaxed ranking.

claim: Combining several estimates beats a single one. Fast Downward multi-heuristic search with preferred operators was best in 23 of 29 domains; LLM heuristic portfolios solved 276 vs 234 of 400 (Tuisov, SP-10 vs first compile); going from 1 to 5 sampled LLM heuristics gave the largest jump (Correa). Caveat from gap search: across nine LLMs on HTN planning the virtual best of five models solved 131 of 139, the same as the best single model (Opus 4, 131), so more models added no coverage there (d03).
agent_test: Generate 2 to 3 different relaxations per problem and rank by agreement; compare to one relaxation at equal tokens. G4: LLM relaxations are correlated, so check the spread.

claim: Landmark counts alone are not competitive; they help when added to an FF-style estimate (LAMA: landmark-only IPC score 164 to 189 vs above 194 combined). Among admissible estimates, landmarks are dominated by additive critical paths and merge-and-shrink.
agent_test: Treat must-happen subgoals as an extra ordering signal only, not the lone score.

claim: Optimal-search quality rises with relaxation accuracy (A* with LM-cut solved 450 tasks vs 422 for landmark h_LA, 314 merge-and-shrink, 294 hmax, 273 blind) but even a near-perfect heuristic leaves exponential search in Gripper-like domains.
agent_test: Not directly testable for a scaffold; a warning that a better relaxed score does not remove search.

claim: Abstraction heuristics (pattern databases) give exact lower bounds from a projected problem at a memory cost: Rubik's Cube tables 42 MB corner, 82 MB total, 10 random cubes solved optimally, median 18 moves.
agent_test: Not an LLM operator. Only lesson: a lookup of solved sub-cases acts as a heuristic.

claim: Writing the heuristic as code and running it in a sound search beats asking the same LLM for the plan. Correa: R1 174 solved end-to-end vs 373 with generated heuristics (720 tasks); Flash 19 vs 296. Tuisov independently reaches state-of-the-art with Rust heuristics from a successor generator (GPT-4.1 SP-10: 276 of 400). Gap search adds cost: V3 $0.25 and R1 $6.12 for 25 heuristics per domain vs $2.79 and $13.62 for end-to-end plans, 200 vs 720 calls (d13); LeanPlan (d01) shows the same code-scorer route with a machine-checked guarantee, but does not compare against LLM plans.
agent_test: Have the model write a scoring function and let code apply it to all children; compare to the model rating children directly, at equal tokens including writing and testing cost.

claim: Thought of Search: the LLM writes the successor function and goal test once and plain search finishes. All 1362 24-game problems solved vs about 75% for Tree of Thoughts on 100 problems with about 100 calls each.
agent_test: Where states are enumerable, ask for code once rather than judging each state.

claim: Example heuristics in the prompt are essential. Gemini Flash Thinking with no example heuristics got coverage 0 for every sample; original prompt best 423, other ablations best 359 to 404.
agent_test: Test the relaxation operator with and without a worked relaxation example for the same class.

claim: Choosing among sampled heuristics on training tasks is lossy. Best of 25 on the test set solved 423 tasks; the selected Gemini Thinking heuristic solved 305 (423/305 = +38.7%). Spread is large (SD 94.3; 64 of 200 failed heuristics). Gap search: a property check on training data with counterexample repair beat sample-and-select (623.3 vs 573 solved of 900; sample-and-select heuristics under hill climbing only 430) with 7.4x fewer generations (d06). A smallest-instance filter removed 361 of 780 candidates unseen (d04).
agent_test: Judge a relaxation by whether its ranking predicts held-out test results; log the rank correlation per problem class.

claim: Part of the LLM-heuristic gain is recall, and on a new domain it shrinks to parity. Obfuscated Blocksworld: R1 heuristic 66 solved vs 40 obfuscated (hFF 27 vs 28). New unreleased Rod-Rings with o3: 58 vs hFF 59. Floortile was the one domain not won by an LLM heuristic. Update: the renamed-domain part still rests on one run. Predicate renaming cut Qwen 2.5-72B direct plan validity from 67.5% to 40.0% (N = 40, d08). On new domains, two other papers with other models are consistent with parity or better (d01, d05); see K25.
agent_test: Evaluate on renamed or novel variants before crediting the relaxation operator.

claim: LLMs used directly as the planner or step chooser are weak without a sound solver. GPT-4 Blocksworld 34.3% (206/600); Mystery 2 to 4.3%; o1-preview 97.8% falls to 52.8% (Mystery) and 23.63% on 20 to 40 step tasks; GPT-4o with PDDL prompts solved 194 of 260 vs 260 for GBFS+hFF and 240 for A*+LM-cut.
agent_test: Never let the model alone certify a relaxed or full plan; code checks.

claim: LLM self-verification is unreliable and a sound checker is better. Blocksworld, 100 instances: generator alone 40, LLM+LLM verifier 55, LLM+VAL 88; the LLM verifier called 38 of 45 wrong plans valid.
agent_test: Already in the schema; a relaxed solve must be checked by code, not by the model.

claim: Worked-example prompting does not generalise beyond the shown examples: gains come only for very specific prompts and decay as block count grows (GPT-4, GPT-4-Turbo, Claude-3-Opus).
agent_test: Check that any relaxation prompt example is not too close to the test cases.

claim: Step-back (ask for the principle first) helps a weaker model on knowledge and physics but little a strong one using chain-of-thought. PaLM-2L Physics 66.4 to 73.2, Chemistry 70.9 to 81.8, TimeQA 41.5 to 66.0, StrategyQA 82.8 to 82.7; GPT-4+CoT 82.9 vs step-back 84.5 on Physics. Over 90% of remaining physics errors are in reasoning, not abstraction.
agent_test: This is abstraction, not relaxation. Test as a cheap S1 step per problem class; do not credit it as relaxation.

claim: Least-to-most (solve easier sub-problems in order) hugely beats chain-of-thought on length generalisation (SCAN, code-davinci-002: 99.7% vs 16.2%; last-letter list 12: 74.0% vs 38.4%) with 14 task-tuned exemplars; other work shows example-specific prompts fade off-distribution.
agent_test: Decomposition is not relaxation. Test on our classes with exemplars not tailored to the test.

claim: Dropping parts of a problem without checking can lose solvability. LLM-pruned grounding: 139 of 175 tasks solved vs 161 for full grounding; 36 of 175 reformulated tasks could not give valid plans for the original; up to two orders of magnitude fewer operators.
agent_test: Any relaxation must be re-checked against the full constraint before acceptance.

claim: Pairing an LLM proposal with a sound relaxation check keeps guarantees. LM-Landmarks (ICML 2026 listing only): LLM-proposed landmarks verified by a delete-relaxation test gave +7.5 coverage points over FF and +3.1 over LAMA, with search nodes down 41% and 37%. Not verified beyond the listing. Gap search: still only the abstract is available; no arm without verification is reported, so the value of verification is not measured (d15).
agent_test: Let the model propose a must-do subgoal, let code check it by relaxed reachability, then use it.

claim: Simplified versions can pull a model to the original's memorised answer. On 97 unpuzzles the gap to the original puzzle was 9.1 points (o3) to 54 points (Gemini 1.5). Gap search: on a 64-item subset, rewriting the simple item in new surface context raised accuracy for every model tested (e.g. GPT-4o 33 to 52, Gemini 2.0 Flash 53 to 70, o3 75 to 80) (d12).
agent_test: When the model solves a relaxed version, check the answer was computed, not recalled; use renamed variants.

claim: No opened paper measures an LLM solving a self-made relaxed version and using it to rank real search children. Closest: code heuristics (Correa, Tuisov), verified landmarks, and AutoCO (LLM-chosen constraint relaxation in optimisation, SFL-8 success 52% to 80%). Gap search 2026-10-26 found no new paper that closes this. Closest new items: h_add rank vs optimal plan length Spearman 0.931 on three held-out domains (d07), but routing needed calibration on 140 real outcomes (d09); a survey finds no ToT work using self-made relaxations (d10).
agent_test: The central open test: relaxed result vs the real child's test result at equal tokens.

claim: LLM-written general plans depend mostly on automatic debugging with checker feedback. GPT-4: Delivery 0.10 without debugging vs 0.90 with; Gripper 0.50 vs 0.90; but Miconic 0.01 and Spanner 0.10 even with it.
agent_test: Reinforces revise-from-real-output; code-writing fails in some domains.

claim: FF's enforced hill-climbing works because a better state is almost always one or two steps away (depth 1 almost always, depth 3 very rarely); in Hanoi it restarts every time. hFF keeps the easy landscape of h+: 220 of 230 instance groups in 11 domains had no sampled valley states; Grid and Hanoi were the exceptions.
agent_test: Commit on the first strictly better child; widen search only when no better child appears within 2 steps (an impasse signal).

claim: LLM-written heuristics stay competitive on never-released domains across several models. LeanPlan (GPT-5.6 Sol, 3 new domains): 67 solved vs 51 for saturated cost partitioning and 11 for LM-cut. Gestrin and Seipp (open-weight models, 8 held-out domains): 368 vs 352 of 720. Correa (o3, Rod-Rings): 58 vs hFF 59. Domain-dependent gains are not all recall, but each paper uses a different setup.
agent_test: Test on unreleased or modified problem variants before crediting the relaxation step; expect parity with the best generic method, not a large gain.

claim: Selecting scorers by checkable property plus counterexample repair beats sampling many and picking by training score. 3.4 candidates per run vs 25; evaluation 10.75 minutes vs 206.25 CPU-hours per domain; 623.3 vs 573 solved of 900 test tasks. Needs a property that code can verify on every training instance.
agent_test: For each scorer, state one property code can check (for example, never ranks a known-failing child above a known-passing one); stop and show the counterexample on the first violation.

claim: Several models or several samples do not guarantee extra coverage once the best candidate is chosen, and model choice dominates. HTN planning: 5-model virtual best 131 = best single model 131 of 139; median expansions differ about 27x between best and worst model. Evolution from a blind seed gave more diverse and higher-ceiling heuristics than from FF (3 of 9 blind runs beat all FF runs). Diversity of starting point helped; extra samples of the same kind did not.
agent_test: Measure agreement between relaxations from one model; if agreement is above chance without gain over one relaxation, stop generating more of the same kind.

claim: A structural relaxed score can rank problem difficulty well without telling which instances a model will solve. h_add reaches Spearman 0.931 with optimal plan length on three held-out domains (N = 126, 164, 133); a threshold fitted on 140 real model outcomes routed 99 to 100% correctly with the best score, but zero-shot routing was 23% to 73%.
agent_test: Calibrate any relaxed rank against the full candidate's real result per problem class before trusting it for pruning.

claim: Heuristics written by a model tend to rediscover known relaxations (FF-like, hadd-like) and gain from corrective penalties for what the relaxation misses. A blind-seeded run produced an FF variant with per-goal penalties (368 vs 352). Reasoning effort raised the share of working programs (73.0% to 83.4% on first try) but not the quality of working ones.
agent_test: Pair each relaxed score with a short must-pass list covering the dropped constraint.

claim: Generated scorers often fail to run at all. HTN: 361 of 780 rejected before testing and 72 of 419 deployed broke on every problem; 60 of those 72 (83%) used the wrong state type. Four of nine LLMs produced a surviving heuristic in only one domain each. In evolved C++ heuristics with three open-weight models, 79.1% worked on the first attempt and 2.5% failed after four attempts.
agent_test: Run a schema and smoke test on every generated scorer on one tiny instance before ranking; count discards in the token cost.

claim: A machine-checked guarantee can be kept with model-written heuristics when the model must also deliver a proof. LeanPlan solved 348 of 1170 tasks with checked admissibility, 281 of 900 IPC 2023 vs 221 for SCP, and refused 3 of 1170 tasks whose assumptions failed. Needs a formal domain; no counterpart for free text yet.
agent_test: Where a property is checkable, have code refuse to use a scorer on any instance that fails the property's preconditions.
